   South Gate Parks & Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting Minutes
  May 9, 2024

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Vice Chair Ruiz

ROLL CALL - by Ana Medina, Sr. Secretary
Present: Chair Alan Flores, Vic Chair Lizette Ruiz, and Secretary Edgar Pelayo.
Staff: Director Steve Costley, Parks Superintendent Glenn Massey, and Recreation Supervisor Donna (Nicki)
Salazar.

APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES
This item was not on the agenda but was included in the Commissioner's packet. Director
Costley asked the Commissioners to review it and give a recommend a motion.
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve the minutes as presented
04/11/24 Minutes M/S/C: Chair Flores/Vice Chair Ruiz to approve the minutes with the correction
of the misspelled word.

PUBLIC COMMENTS
Recognized: Mario Dominguez, SG resident, expressed how upset he is that the meetings no longer will be
via Zoom.

OPEN SESSION ITEMS

1. REVIEW OF 3RD QUARTER RECREATION PROGRAMS FY 2023/24
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz to keep the board as is with Commissioner Pelayo as
Secretary.
Supervisor Salazar reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Vice Chair Ruiz asked about pickle ball;
Recreation Supv. Salazar explained that it was a one-time special event, but staff are looking to offer it in
the summer. Also, on the status of the SELA Art Center; have met with them but nothing certain yet.
Secretary Pelayo asked on the capacity of the swim stadium for meets; Director Costley said that there's
seating for 600 in the bleachers, usually the teams set up at the outside deck. He mentioned that seniors
are not tech savvy; Recreation Supv. Salazar said staff is creating a senior board to gather info and looking
into workshops to teach them. What is the City's input on SELA and are there any partnerships. Director
Costley explained they are separate from the City and there aren't any partnerships. Chair Flores offered
his social media to help promote the Parks events and activities.

2. REVIEW OF 3RD QUARTER GROUNDS & FACILITY MAINTENANCE FY 2023/24
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Secretary Pelayo
Parks Supt. Massey reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Vice Chair Ruiz is happy the North Playground
has been upgraded; the Earth Day events were good, it's good to see the community involved. Chair Flores
and Secretary Pelayo both expressed how good the parks look and thanked staff for their work.

  Page 1 of 3
  4
 3. ANNUAL REVIEW OF CONCESSION AGREEMENTS
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/ Vice Chair Ruiz
Director Costley explained this item; a discussion ensued. Vice Chair Ruiz asked about Sofive's repairs to
the batting cages; Director Costley explained that it would cost a lot to do them all at once so they are
repairing individual machines and the nets. Asked about their intent to sell alcohol, Director Costley
explained the process. He also stated that they allocate several hours for the department and public to use
the soccer center. They also provide time at the batting cages for classes and JAA use. Secretary Pelayo
asked if the Parks will get any revenue from the alcohol sales, Director Costley stated that would be
decided through Community Development and Planning. Chair Flores asked if there could be a Saturday
Farmers Market, Director Costley explained that they already have other locations on Saturday.

4. APPROVAL OF PROPOSED MEETING SCHEDULE FOR FY 2024/25
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve the proposed meeting schedule with any suggested changes
for the coming fiscal year.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz to approve the proposed meeting schedule with Secretary
Pelayo's requested changes.
Director Costley explained this item; a discussion ensued. Secretary Pelayo asked if the Parks Master Plan
could be moved up to July and Vice Chair Ruiz asked to have a safety report done in August.

Recognized: Mario Dominguez, SG resident, is not happy with the delays with the Parks Master Plan

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Director Costley: This year's JAA Opening Day on May 4, will be Gil's last year as president of the
organization. The fencing project might be completed by the middle of June, there have been several
delays because of the rain. This year the Senior Ball was held at the Commerce Casino because attendance
has gone up to 600. Public Works staff are continuing repair work on the AC in the Sports Center.

Parks Supt. Massey: Just the usual; staff is gearing up for the summer season.

Recreation Supervisor Salazar: Reported on upcoming events. The Spring Fit 5K has 950 registered
participants; Memorial Day Ceremonies will be Saturday, May 25 at 10am at the Veteran's Memorial
Fountain. Concerts in the Park series will begin on July 5 for the next four Fridays, then the Movies in the
Park series to follow on Saturdays; the Fun Run will be on July 20. A new event, Camp Out, will be August
3.

PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION SUB-COMMITTEE REPORTS
Chair Flores: Asked why there are only Spanish music bands? Recreation Supv. Salazar explained that
English music has been done in the past but they didn't attract many people; looking into getting a wider
range of different types of Spanish music. Secretary Pelayo mentioned that some Mariachi groups play
English songs.

Vice Chair Ruiz: Will be participating in the 5K.

Secretary Pelayo: How many SG residents were at the Senior Ball? Director Costley explained that the Ball
is a joint effort with several cities, each city has 50 participants.

ADJOURNMENT - At 8:45 p.m. Chair Flores asked for a motion to adjourn.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz

Respectfully submitted:

Edgar Pelayo, Secretary

   Parks & Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
  July 11, 2024
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Nicki Salazar, Recreation Supervisor
Date:  June 12, 2024
Subject:  Social & Cultural Division Report for FY 2023/24

Recommended Motion:  Motion to Receive and File

Report Summary:

Special Events: Fiscal year 2023/24 kicked off summer with our Concerts in the Park
series. This family friendly event invited community members to enjoy every Friday
evening with us at the South Gate Park Bandstand. The series offered 4 musical
groups the opportunity to showcase their musical talents and bring the crowd alive.
Week 1 began with “Mariachi Espectacular”, Week 2 was “All the Vibes Band”, Week 3
was “Here 4 Now” and the series concluded with the “Mariachi Divas”. Our concert
series has continued to see a slight increase with overall participation at 250-300 people
per concert. One new addition this year was food trucks and a beer garden being
onsite for the last concert of the series.

Movies in the Park was hosted every Friday evening in August at the South Gate Golf
Course. Participants enjoyed an evening under the stars and some quality family time
while enjoying the following films: Puss in Boots, Turning Red, Nacho Libre, and
Minions.

Halloween Haunt 2023 was held on Tuesday, October 31, from 6-9pm in the large quad
located in South Gate Park. The event had over 35 engaging and interactive game
booths where patrons could play and receive toys and/or candy. Photo opportunities
were spread throughout the event so patrons could take photos with their friends and
family. DJ Gilbert was playing the hottest tunes and had the crowd pumped up; we held
our costume contests and numerous dance competitions for patrons to receive goodie
bags. The Halloween Haunt also brought back our children’s jumper area with a total of
three jumpers for kids to play on. Lastly, the event had our trackless trains offering
rides to over the 5,000 people in attendance.

Veterans Day took place on Saturday, November 11, from 11am to 1pm at South Gate
Park. There was a total of 75 people in attendance, with light refreshments and pastries
being distributed. Every Veteran in attendance was gifted a medal and hat. The Legacy
Cadet Corp from Legacy High School and the K-Kids from Willow Elementary
  Page 1 of 5  17
 participated in the event by assisting with the Call to Honor, leading the pledge of
allegiance, and reading letters to Veterans.

Winter Wonderland was held in conjunction with Police Navidad on Tuesday, December
5, from 4 to 8pm at South Gate City Hall. Over 900 wristbands were distributed to
children to participate in the night’s activities. Wristbands allowed access to the
following areas: snowball fight, snow play, snow globe photo station, and the small &
large sled runs. In addition to the activities, each child with a wristband also received a
gift from Santa. Parents were able to get it on the action and enjoyed free churros and
hot chocolate while their children enjoyed the evening.

Santa’s Breakfast closed out the holiday season and was hosted on Saturday,
December 9, from 9am to 1pm at the Henry C. Gonzalez Auditorium. This event SOLD
OUT and had a total of 300 registered participants. Those in attendance were served
breakfast consisting of sausage, pancakes, milk, and orange juice. Children attending
the event participated in two craft areas and were able to write letters to Santa and
place them in Santa’s mailbox. Lastly, each child was gifted their own gingerbread
house kit and was able to take pictures with Santa and the Grinch. Raffles ended the
event with the chance to win gift cards, two bikes, and three Christmas trees.

Easterfest is the last special event of the fiscal year and took place on Saturday, March
23, from 10am to 1pm. It was scheduled to take place at the South Gate Golf Course,
however, due to rain, the event was moved into the South Gate Sports Center. The
event included multiple stations: jumpers, a toddler soft play area, face painting, ballon
twister, arts/ crafts game boothsm and a photo area with the Easter Bunny. Children
were also able to participate in egg hunts that accommodated the different age groups
to ensure safety. The egg hunts were separated from ages 2-3 years old (one parent
was allowed to assist the child during the egg hunt) 4-5 years old, 6-8 years old, 9 and
over. Children were also given the opportunity to find a golden egg, (2 per egg hunt
age) winners were awarded an Easter basket filled with toys, candy, and other special
prizes! Lastly, what is an event without snow cones; we had the Kona Ice truck parked
outside of the Sports Center for any patrons who wanted to purchase sweet treats.

Youth Programs: ABC’s and 123’s are taught in our Tiny Two’s and Tot Time classes.
Each quarter this year we offered a total of seven classes and every class was filled.
Tiny Two’s classes focused on introducing children to the classroom setting and
encouraging socialization. Parent involvement is required for Tiny Two’s and each
registered participant must have one adult attend class with them every day. Tot time
classes focused on teaching the children their numbers, colors, and shapes. Each nine-
week session ended with a themed party ranging from movie day to pajama parties.
During our summer and spring sessions students also had the opportunity to attend
excursions to Wild Rivers and the LA County fair.

In addition to our preschool programs our youth programming team brought back our
popular Lil Chefs class. Lil Chefs is a 5-week program that allows registrants the
opportunity to prepare and execute new recipes every week. Staff chooses a main
course and snack/dessert to prepare each week. Registrants are taught safety rules in
the kitchen and kitchen etiquette when preparing the recipes. Recipes included:
meatball subs, chicken nuggets from scratch, enchilada casserole, green smoothies,
  Page 2 of 5  18
 zucchini pizza bowls, and cake pops. It is safe to say that every registrant left each
class happy and full.

Teen Programming: “Teen Glow” was the marquee event of the year for our teen
programming section. Local teens from across the SELA region made the trek to the
South Gate Golf Course to enjoy a night full of fun activities. As soon as participants
arrived, they were greeted by our team and all the glow swag one could wish for. Each
teen had the opportunity to participate in the glow golf tournament, laser tag,
photobooth, and dance floor. DJ Charles Boogie was on the 1’s & 2’s playing the
hottest hits while getting our teens out of their comfort zone and making their way to the
dance floor. In addition to all the offered amenities each participant received pizza,
chips, dessert, and a beverage of their choice.

As we continue to re-build the Teen Programming section, we were also able to provide
one excursion to Knotts Scary Farm. Participants loaded onto buses and enjoyed a
frightful evening surrounded by friends, ghouls, and monsters. Lastly, our team began
its preliminary stage of rebuilding our Teen Center and developing the programming to
come along with it. Staff had the opportunity to table at our local high school events,
which allowed our team to connect directly with our target audience. Staff created an
interest list of participants so once we do get our programming back up and running, we
have a core group of teens to reach out to.

Senior Services: Our Senior Center is dedicated to offering a diverse range of
activities, programs, excursions, and services. Our programming is all about promoting
health, well-being, and lifelong learning. Complimentary to our programming our Senior
Center is also a facility that encourages new friendships and socialization. Every month
the Senior Center hosts holiday parties, where everyone comes together to enjoy each
other’s company surrounded by themed decorations and refreshments. Bingo & Loteria
are crowd favorites and a staple in our programming, all participants show up ready to
play and fill up the main hall. To stay active we offer yoga, two days a week and our
very own blue jays dance group meets three times a week. If you really want to join the
party, Thursdays are the day; karaoke and dancing are always a hit as our seniors
dress up for an afternoon on the town.

Each year our Senior Center team is part of the Annual Southeast Senior Ball, this
event originated here in South Gate and has grown exponentially over the years. This
event is now hosted between 12 participating cities and was recognized and awarded at
this year’s California Parks and Recreation Conference in Palm Springs. This event is
hosted at the Commerce Casino; each city charters in 50 of their own seniors to enjoy a
catered lunch, coffee bar, photo booth, giveaways and many memorable experiences.

Partner organizations who provide services to our seniors are a crucial part of
programming. Two meal programs are available at our Senior Center: HSA and Meals
on Wheels. HSA Senior Lunch Program offers daily hot meals onsite, Monday thru
Friday with a suggested donation of $2.25. For any seniors who are unable to visit us in
person, Meals on Wheels is the program for them. Seniors can contact the organization
directly and will be provided with meals for the entire week. Another service available to

  Page 3 of 5  19
 our seniors is a partnership with LA County Mental health. This group meets every
Tuesday and Thursday after lunch to allow the seniors time to share experiences and
ensure their mental health is being supported.

Lastly, community excursions are always successful, and every trip reaches maximum
capacity, this year was no different. Some of the excursions provided this year
included: Solvang, Catalina Island, OC Fair, Musicals, Disney on Ice, Medieval times,
Balloon & Wine Festivals, Hollywood Bowl, and Casinos galore. Excursion pricing
varies depending on the trip, but with transportation being provided to and from each
destination, these excursions really are a steal.

Contract Classes: Consistency is key with contract classes; this year solidified our
core group of offerings at the Girls Club House. If your child was looking for an active
class then we were sure to have it. The bulk of programming is geared towards getting
our children moving and we offered many different classes to accomplish that goal:
baby boogie, folklorico, ballet, hip hop, tumbling, cheerleading, and self-defense.
Multiple offerings per week make it very easy for any of our community members to be
able to find something that accommodates their family's schedule. For children and
teens who have an artistic interest we also have an art class as well as a fashion
sketching class available. Registration for these classes typically reaches maximum
capacity every quarter and that is due to the curriculum and amazing contractors we
currently work with.

At the end of every quarter, participants do have the option to perform in our dance
recitals. Dance recitals are held at the end of the nine-week session and the students
are able to showcase their new skills and dance routines they learned. Each participant
receives two complimentary tickets for entrance and have the ability to purchase more
for their extended family members as well. All recitals are held in the Henry C.
Gonzalez Auditorium and are spread across three nights with an audience of 350-500
each night. Our participants and their families really enjoy these recitals as it is the
culmination of their nine weeks of hard work and dedication.

Golf Course: The action on the Golf Course this year was consistent, we had a great
balance of our everyday regulars and had the opportunity to host a ton of new faces. In
addition to the daily golfers, our local high schools continued to host their practices and
matches on our course as well. Not only did our golfers get to come and play their 9-
holes on a well-maintained green golf course, but they also had many new updated
items to enjoy along the way. This year we were able to purchase and install brand new
pole and flag combos for all 9-holes and the putting greens. We installed new ball
washers, spike cleaners, and purchased six brand new push golf carts. Keeping on
trend with the new additions and overall improvement of the Golf Course, we were also
able to re-design new scorecards that display a course map and our own City of South
Gate Golf Course logo. Lastly, our driving range has re-opened after being closed for a
few years, we had damaged poles replaced and all new netting installed.

Cultural Arts: This year our Cultural Arts team created and hosted three art exhibits:
Proceso - Process, Héroe Locale - Home Town Hero and Oír de Nuevo - Press Repeat.

  Page 4 of 5  20
 Each exhibit had an opening reception, remained open for two months and concluded
with a closing reception. During open hours, artists and visitors were able to immerse
themselves in the art, observe/ reflect on all pieces, ask questions and network with
other local artists. All exhibits received and displayed a wide range of submissions and
showcased local talent. In addition to the art exhibits our team hosted the 3 rd Annual Art
Walk which was composed of over 56 vendors/artisans/artists displaying/vending their
work. In collaboration with five partner organizations' leading art workshops, we also
had two DJs (one on the main stage and one in front of the courthouse), three bands’
(performances on the main stage/show mobile), and three live artists drawing/painting.
The Art Walk was well attended and had over 500 community members who enjoyed an
afternoon full of art and culture.

The inspiration did not stop there, workshops and classes were also a huge success for
our Cultural Arts team. Zine Fiesta 2 was offered, and artists had the opportunity to
create new networks, share ideas and collaborate on writing and artwork. During our
month-long Azalea Festival, the team collaborated with the South Gate Art Association
and had three interactive booths during Family Art Night. In addition to the booths our
team was able to provide a free dance performance in conjunction with The Music
Center Arts Grown LA and Ballet Folklorico de Brasil was onstage and pumping up the
crowd. Lastly, enrollment for a majority of the classes remained steady. Art Club, oil
painting, drawing + comics, and watercolor painting were the favorites and we were able
to see many repeat customers who were delighted with their experience.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 3

To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Deputy Director
Date:  June 18, 2024

Subject:  Annual Report on Implementation of the Parks & Recreation Master Plan

Recommended Motion:  Motion to Approve and Report to City Council

Report Summary: A Parks & Recreation Master Plan for South Gate was approved by
the Parks & Recreation Commission and adopted by the City Council in November 2008.
As part of the implementation process for the Parks Master Plan, the Commission is
required to report to the City Council annually as to the progress that has been made in
achieving the goals that were outlined. The following report shows that progress. If
approved, staff will forward the report to the City Council on behalf of the Commission.

This will be the last update report for the Parks & Recreation Commission on the Master
Plan. After 15 years, the City Council has authorized a “New” Master Plan be developed for
the Parks & Recreation Department that receives input from current residents and
stakeholders and allows input from our ever-changing community. The RFP process and
scheduling for the updated Master Plan is scheduled to start at the end of 2024 and will
involve the Parks & Recreation Commission in the process.

As for 2023/24 it was a busy year with pushing projects toward completion and finding
funding for those items in the que.

To this end, we have received substantial funding this year from several different sources,
for several different projects. Some of the funding is directly tied to a single project, while
other funding is able to be used on a variety of projects. Here is what we have received to
date:

•  Hollydale Community  Prop. 68  $4,158,942

Goals of the Parks & Recreation Master Plan.
The Parks & Recreation Master Plan contains 133 individual recommendations for actions,
improvements or projects to be implemented. This list was summarized into nine priority
goals. Here is an update on the overall progress.

  1.  Replace existing restrooms in parks that have not had their restrooms
  replaced.
New restrooms at State Street Park, South Gate Park and Circle Park have been
completed.

  2.  Protect and upgrade existing facilities through allocation of resources
  including:
Upgrades to existing facilities have been on-going throughout the entire process. These
include renovation of the Auditorium, Swim Stadium, and Sports Center Roof as well as
replacement of picnic areas and several playgrounds plus many more projects.

  3.  Develop and implement a specific plan for the eastern corridor of South Gate
  Park from Tweedy Blvd north to Southern Ave along Pinehurst St. to
  accommodate additional sports fields, an event plaza, a new Boy Scout
  Lodge, batting cages, revenue generating commercial sports facility, and
  associated additional parking.

The addition of the Goals Soccer Center and Batting Cages has completed a portion of this
goal. While a new “Scout Lodge” was concepted, it was not received well by the Boy
Scouts.
  4.  Increase trails, open space and recreational opportunities on the west side
  through the following:
Completed upgrades at Cesar Chavez Park and used the land on Southern Avenue to
implement State Street Park.

  5.  Expand teen opportunities in the community by including teen specific

  Page 2 of 3
  23
   activities at the proposed events plaza, teen sports leagues and programs at
  the proposed sports center concession and the eventual establishment of a
  dedicated teen center.

The new Teen Center was in full operation in 2016. A variety of teen centered programs
have been offered but due in part to cultural changes, technology and Covid, the Teen
Center was closed and Teen Programming has been slow to recover.
  6.  Create a perimeter and internal trail system at South Gate Park to provide
  formal walking, jogging and exercise paths, pedestrian connections to all
  park venues from all parking areas, and a connection to a citywide trails
  system.

The perimeter trail at South Gate Park has long been established. In 2016, at the
recommendation of the Parks & Recreation Commission, dogs have now been allowed, on
leash, on this perimeter trail expanding its existing uses.

  7.  Replace existing Park Maintenance Yard in order to implement the
  recommended aggressive park maintenance program.

While the overall Park Maintenance Yard was not replaced due to lack of space,
renovations were completed for the roof and parking bays in the facility.

  8.  Undertake refurbishment and recommended improvements to Hollydale
  Regional Park, renaming it Hollydale Community Park to reflect more
  appropriate context of its use.

A site master plan was completed in 2016 for all three of the Hollydale Parks. We are
currently in the process of completing renovation of Hollydale Community Park and Circle
Park. Hollydale Regional Park has some preliminary plans but lacks the overall funding to
move forward.
  9.  Expand swimming pool facilities to include new uses for revenue generation.

Work on the repair of the roof and replacement of the existing skylights was completed in
2017. Hours were expanded to include 6 am openings and Friday usage.

Summary
Staff believes that the past fifteen years represent significant progress in achieving the
goals of the Parks Master plan. Cities often take time and money to put together a Master
Plan for their Parks & Recreation Department and after some initial “hoopla” the plan gets
put in a binder and placed on a shelf never to be opened again. This is not the case for the
City of South Gate. Our Master Plan has for fifteen years been a living, breathing,
document that has been updated/revised every 5 years and become a fundamental
planning tool for the Department. Our hope is that the next Master Plan provides as much
guidance as this one has for the residents of South Gate.
